scene_summary: A gallery photograph rather than a minimal expressionist scene: a large lavender-grey painting fills the left side, while a standing visitor holding a bag occupies the right above a wooden floor. The turned lavender field is clearly present. A lower dark pigment interruption and a small bag-webbing junction offer qualified secondary targets. The planned folded aperture, rubbed floor abrasion, and illuminated upper plaster seam are not visibly established; neither the ordinary frame nor cast shadows should substitute for those missing marks.

detected_objects.label: Turned lavender field
detected_objects.visual_evidence: The actual painted surface is a large perspective-skewed plane, clipped by the top and left image boundaries and bounded by a thin brown frame at right and bottom. Lavender patchwork surrounds an orange star field and green-black stripes. The motif belongs to this same source window, not a second gallery-image window.

detected_objects.label: Lower dark pigment interruption
detected_objects.visual_evidence: An irregular charcoal patch interrupts the lower-right portion of the lavender painting, below a pale transverse break in the tall dark stripe. Its ragged lower edge meets a small blue accent. This is a visible pigment target, but only a partial match for Broad pigment fall: it is narrow and vertically weighted, not the planned broad blurred botanical smear. It is nested inside the primary painted plane and would require interaction priority over that larger window.

complexity_assessment.rationale: Estimated coverage describes the visible union of mapped surfaces, not summed overlapping polygons. The composition has generous quiet wall space, but its photographic visitor, detailed bag, wood grain, distressed painting, and repeated stars and stripes prevent a minimal expressionist reading. Only one planned anchor is unequivocal and two have qualified visible counterparts. No distinct folded picture aperture, bounded rubbed floor patch, or short illuminated upper plaster seam is visible. Adding windows to reach six would require arbitrary substitutions.
